name: Amogh
tagline: I study why materials fail, and how to make them better — on the bench, in simulation, and on the fretboard.

intro.short: Metallurgical & Materials Engineering graduate (VNIT Nagpur), now pursuing an M.Tech in Computational Materials Engineering at IIT Bombay. My core interests — physical metallurgy, failure analysis, and materials characterization — haven't changed; I'm extending them into computational modeling, connecting predicted microstructure back to real experimental behavior.
intro.long: I'm a Metallurgical & Materials Engineering graduate from VNIT Nagpur, now pursuing an M.Tech in Computational Materials Engineering at IIT Bombay. My work so far has been mostly experimental — SEM fractography, mechanical testing, investment casting — and the questions I kept running into were computational ones: given a microstructure, can I predict how and where it'll fail before I ever pull a specimen. That's the gap I'm working on now, through ICME-style modeling — CALPHAD-informed alloy design, phase-field microstructure evolution, and machine-learned interatomic potentials standing in for expensive DFT — while staying grounded in the experimental characterization I already know how to do. Outside the lab, I play guitar — acoustic and electric, mostly chasing tone and recording covers and collaborations rather than technical shredding.
